items.title: The Preschooler Drawing Experiment
items.content_snippet: The danger was never the reward. It was the promise. The moment something you love becomes something you're owed for, the love quietly leaves. The detail that makes it land: it wasn't the prize that did the damage. The children who got a surprise reward afterward kept drawing as much as ever. items.title: How Financial Planners With Zero Coding Experience Built Their Own Agents - Matt Ragone, Range
items.content_snippet: Matt Ragone is a financial planner at Range, an all-in-one wealth management firm, not an engineer. He leads AI adoption for its planning team and shares the step-by-step method non-technical planners used to build their own agents and skills. items.title: Your Coding Agent Can't Undo Its Own Mistakes - Tanmay Sah & Dolly Sah
items.content_snippet: Tanmay Sah and Dolly Sah look at a capability today's coding agents are missing: undoing what they've done. Drawing on their research projects UndoBench and EvoUndo, they show that an agent that completes a task can't necessarily put things back when something breaks, because Git doesn't cover external API calls, runtime config or notifications, and retrying doesn't reverse side effects. In EvoUndo, 197 of 478 changes that made an agent more capable (about 42%) also broke its ability to recover.

items.title: Your Company Has No Model of Itself. Agents Can Build One - Joao Wenzel, Citadel Securities
items.content_snippet: Every company has someone who knows everything: the reorgs, the politics, which projects are really on track. Joao Wenzel of Citadel Securities explains how his team approximates that person with an agentic system that builds an institutional memory from decks, Slack, meeting notes, code changes and agent traces.
